label: ass:4.5
title: Assumption
body_md:
\label{ass:4.5}
At every accumulation point $x^\star$ of the primal sequence, the
gradients of the active equality and inequality constraints are
linearly independent. Moreover, in a neighborhood of each relevant
accumulation point, the active-set KKT systems associated with the
local SQP and SQCQP subproblems are strongly regular, with a uniformly bounded local inverse-Lipschitz modulus.
Let $(\widehat{\lambda}^k,\widehat{\mu}^k)$ denote the local multiplier pair associated with the effective direction $d^k$ passed to globalization. Along every relevant convergent subsequence,
\[\|\widehat{\lambda}^k-\lambda^k\|_2+\|\widehat{\mu}^k-\mu^k\|_2\longrightarrow0. \]

Furthermore, every corresponding accumulation point $(x^\star,\lambda^\star,\mu^\star)$ satisfies the second-order sufficient condition
\[w^\top\nabla_{xx}^2\mathcal{L}(x^\star,\lambda^\star,\mu^\star)w>0\]
for every nonzero direction $w$ in the associated critical cone.
head: environment
name: Local regularity and multiplier consistency

label: lem:4.1
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:4.1}
Suppose Assumptions~\ref{ass:4.1} and~\ref{ass:4.2} hold. At every non-refresh iteration \(k\), $e^k=e^{k-1}+\xi^k,$ where
$\xi^k=\left[\nabla F_{\mathcal{B}_k}(x^k)-\nabla F_{\mathcal{B}_k}(x^{k-1})\right]-\left[\nabla F(x^k)-\nabla F(x^{k-1})\right].$
Moreover,
\[\mathbb{E}\left[\xi^k\mid\mathcal{F}_{k-1}\right]=0,and \
\left[\|\xi^k\|_2^2\mid\mathcal{F}_{k-1}\right]\leq\frac{L_F^2}{b_k}\|x^k-x^{k-1}\|_2^2.\]
head: environment
name: SPIDER error recursion and conditional variance

title: Proof
body_md:
At a non-refresh iteration, $g^k=\nabla F_{\mathcal{B}_k}(x^k)-\nabla F_{\mathcal{B}_k}(x^{k-1})+g^{k-1}.$ Subtracting \(\nabla F(x^k)\), and adding and subtracting\(\nabla F(x^{k-1})\), gives\[e^k=e^{k-1}+\xi^k.\]
The conditional zero-mean property follows directly from the unbiased
mini-batch sampling in Assumption~\ref{ass:4.2}.
For the variance bound, define\[\Delta_r^k=\nabla F_r(x^k)-\nabla F_r(x^{k-1}).\]
The mini-batch gradient difference is the sample average of \(\Delta_r^k\), whereas its population mean is $\overline{\Delta}^k=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{r=1}^{N}\Delta_r^k=\nabla F(x_k)-\nabla F(x_{k-1}).$
Using the standard variance bound for uniform mini-batch sampling and
Assumption~\ref{ass:4.1},\[\|\Delta_r^k\|_2\leq L_F\|x^k-x^{k-1}\|_2,\]which yields
\[\mathbb{E}\left[\|\xi^k\|_2^2\mid\mathcal{F}_{k-1}\right]\leq\frac{L_F^2}{b_k}
\|x^k-x^{k-1}\|_2^2.\]
head: environment

label: thm:spider_consistency
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:spider_consistency}
Suppose Assumptions~\ref{ass:4.1} and~\ref{ass:4.2} hold and that
$\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}\|x^k-x^{k-1}\|_2^2\right]<\infty.$
Then\[\|g^k-\nabla F(x^k)\|_2\longrightarrow0\qquad\text{a.s.}\]
head: environment
name: Almost-sure consistency of the SPIDER estimator

title: Proof
body_md:
Let \(s(k)\) denote the most recent refresh iteration at or before \(k\). Since the refresh period \(q\) is finite by construction, $0\leq k-s(k)\leq q-1,$  and $e^{s(k)}=0.$ Repeated application of Lemma~\ref{lem:4.1} therefore gives
\[e^k=\sum_{j=s(k)+1}^{k}\xi^j.\]
Since the increments are conditionally centered, the cross terms vanish in expectation. Hence, by Lemma~\ref{lem:4.1},\[\mathbb{E}\|e^k\|_2^2\leq L_F^2 \sum_{j=s(k)+1}^{k}\mathbb{E}\|x^j-x^{j-1}\|_2^2.\]
Each iterate difference occurs in at most \(q\) such refresh windows,and therefore
\[\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}\mathbb{E}\|e^k\|_2^2\leq qL_F^2 \mathbb{E}\left[ \sum_{k=1}^{\infty} \|x^k-x^{k-1}\|_2^2\right]<\infty.\]
For every \(\varepsilon>0\), Markov's inequality gives
\[\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}\mathbb{P}\left(\|e^k\|_2>\varepsilon\right)<\infty.\]
The first Borel--Cantelli lemma then implies $\|e^k\|_2\longrightarrow0\ \text{a.s.},$ which proves the result.
head: environment

label: cor:4.1
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:4.1}
Under the conditions of Theorem~\ref{thm:spider_consistency},
\[\left\|\nabla_x\mathcal{L}^k-\nabla_x\mathcal{L}(x^k,\lambda^k,\mu^k)\right\|_2
\longrightarrow0\qquad\text{a.s.}\]
head: environment
name: Stochastic Lagrangian-gradient consistency

title: Proof
body_md:
By the definitions of the stochastic and exact Lagrangian gradients,
\[
abla_x\mathcal{L}^k-
abla_x\mathcal{L}(x^k,\lambda^k,\mu^k)=g^k-
abla F(x^k)
=e^k.\]The result follows immediately from Theorem~ef{thm:spider_consistency}.
head: environment

label: lem:4.2
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:4.2}
Suppose Assumptions~\ref{ass:4.1}, \ref{ass:4.3}, and \ref{ass:4.5} hold. Consider a relevant convergent subsequence lying in the local regular regime of Assumption~\ref{ass:4.5}, and suppose that the SQP and SQCQP subproblems share the locally identified active set \(\mathcal{A}_k\). Then there exist constants
\(C_{\mathrm{dir}}>0\) and \(\delta_d>0\) such that, whenever $\|d_{\mathrm{SQP}}^k\|_2\leq\delta_d,$ the corresponding SQCQP direction satisfies
\[\boxed{\left\|d_{\mathrm{SQCQP}}^k-d_{\mathrm{SQP}}^k\right\|_2\leq C_{\mathrm{dir}}\left\|d_{\mathrm{SQP}}^k\right\|_2.}\]
Consequently,
$d_{\mathrm{SQP}}^k\longrightarrow0 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad d_{\mathrm{SQCQP}}^k\longrightarrow0.$
head: environment
name: Local SQP--SQCQP direction stability

title: Proof
body_md:
The SQCQP KKT residual is first evaluated at the SQP KKT pair.Using the SQP stationarity and active-constraint equations, we get
\[\Psi^k\left(d_{\mathrm{SQP}}^k,\nu_{\mathrm{SQP}}^k\right)=\begin{bmatrix}
(G^k-B^k)d_{\mathrm{SQP}}^k+H^k(\nu_{\mathrm{SQP}}^k)d_{\mathrm{SQP}}^k\\[1mm]
q^k(d_{\mathrm{SQP}}^k)\end{bmatrix}.\]
By Assumption~\ref{ass:4.3}, $\|G^k-B^k\|_2\leq\overline g+\overline b.$
Along the convergent subsequence, the outer multipliers are bounded, and the multiplier consistency in Assumption~\ref{ass:4.5} therefore implies boundedness of the corresponding local multipliers which is proved later in \ref{lem:4.6}. Together with the bounded constraint Hessians in Assumption~\ref{ass:4.1}, there exists \(C_H>0\) such that \[\left\|H^k(\nu_{\mathrm{SQP}}^k)\right\|_2\leq C_H.\]
Similarly, bounded constraint curvature gives a constant \(C_q>0\) such that
\[\left\|q^k(d_{\mathrm{SQP}}^k)\right\|_2\leq C_q\left\|d_{\mathrm{SQP}}^k \right\|_2^2.\]
Hence, for suitable constants \(C_1,C_2>0\),
\[\left\|\Psi^k\left(d_{\mathrm{SQP}}^k,\nu_{\mathrm{SQP}}^k\right)\right\|_2\leq
C_1\left\|d_{\mathrm{SQP}}^k\right\|_2+C_2\left\|d_{\mathrm{SQP}}^k\right\|_2^2.\]
For sufficiently small \(\|d_{\mathrm{SQP}}^k\|_2\), the quadratic term is dominated by the linear term, so that
\[\left\|\Psi^k\left(d_{\mathrm{SQP}}^k,\nu_{\mathrm{SQP}}^k\right)\right\|_2\leq
C\left\|d_{\mathrm{SQP}}^k\right\|_2\] for some \(C>0\).

By the strong regularity stated in Assumption~\ref{ass:4.5}, the locally identified SQCQP KKT system possesses a locally Lipschitz inverse with uniformly bounded modulus. Therefore, for some \(C_{\mathrm{reg}}>0\),
\[\left\|z_{\mathrm{SQCQP}}^k-z_{\mathrm{SQP}}^k\right\|_2\leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}
\left\|\Psi^k\left(d_{\mathrm{SQP}}^k,\nu_{\mathrm{SQP}}^k\right)\right\|_2.\]
Combining the preceding bounds yields
\[\left\|z_{\mathrm{SQCQP}}^k-z_{\mathrm{SQP}}^k\right\|_2\leq C_{\mathrm{dir}}
\left\|d_{\mathrm{SQP}}^k\right\|_2\]
for some \(C_{\mathrm{dir}}>0\). Since the primal direction is a component of the KKT vector \(z\),
\[\left\|d_{\mathrm{SQCQP}}^k-d_{\mathrm{SQP}}^k\right\|_2\leq C_{\mathrm{dir}}
\left\|d_{\mathrm{SQP}}^k\right\|_2.\]
Finally, $\|d_{\mathrm{SQCQP}}^k\|_2\leq\left(1+C_{\mathrm{dir}}\right)
\|d_{\mathrm{SQP}}^k\|_2,$ which proves that \(d_{\mathrm{SQP}}^k\to0\) implies \(d_{\mathrm{SQCQP}}^k\to0\).
head: environment

label: lem:4.3
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Stochastic merit-function remainder

title: Proof
body_md:
By the Lipschitz continuity of \(\nabla F\) in Assumption~\ref{ass:4.1}, the descent lemma gives\[F(x^k+\alpha d^k)\leq F(x^k) + \alpha\nabla F(x^k)^\top d^k + \frac{L_F}{2}\alpha^2\|d^k\|_2^2.\]
Since $\nabla F(x^k)=g^k-e^k,$ Cauchy--Schwarz yields
\[F(x^k+\alpha d^k)\leq F(x^k)+\alpha(g^k)^\top d^k+\alpha\|e^k\|_2\|d^k\|_2
+\frac{L_F}{2}\alpha^2\|d^k\|_2^2.\]
It remains to control the constraint-violation term. Taylor's theorem and the Hessian bounds in Assumption~\ref{ass:4.1} imply, for each equality constraint,
\[|h_i(x^k+\alpha d^k)|\leq|h_i(x^k)|+\alpha D|h_i(x^k)|[d^k]+\frac{M_h}{2} \alpha^2\|d^k\|_2^2.\]
Likewise, using the one-sided directional derivative of the positive-part mapping,
\[c_j(x^k+\alpha d^k)^+\leq c_j(x^k)^+ +\alpha Dc_j(x^k)^+[d^k]+\frac{M_c}{2}
\alpha^2\|d^k\|_2^2.\]
Summation over all constraints gives
\[V(x^k+\alpha d^k)\leq V(x^k)+\alpha DV(x^k)[d^k]+\frac{mM_h+pM_c}{2} \alpha^2\|d^k\|_2^2.\]
Multiplying this inequality by \(\rho_k\), adding the objective bound, and using the definition of \(D_k^\Phi\) gives\eqref{eq:stochastic_merit_remainder}.
head: environment

label: lem:4.4
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:4.4}
Suppose Assumption~\ref{ass:4.3} holds and that the local SQP and SQCQP subproblems admit the relevant KKT solutions. At any nonstationary iteration for which the effective direction is nonzero, the AVR-SS(QC)QP globalization procedure obtains, after finitely many within-iteration penalty adjustments, $D_k^\Phi<0.$
head: environment
name: Finite construction of an effective merit-descent direction

title: Proof
body_md:
Consider first an RCMCI-selected SQCQP candidate. If its stochastic merit directional quantity is already negative, no modification is required.
Suppose instead that $D_k^\Phi\geq0.$ If $DV(x^k)[d_{\mathrm{SQCQP}}^k]\geq0,$ increasing the penalty parameter cannot create descent. By the globalization safeguard, the SQCQP candidate is therefore replaced by the already-computed SQP probe and its associated local multipliers. If, on the other hand, $DV(x^k)[d_{\mathrm{SQCQP}}^k]<0,$ then, with the direction held fixed, $D_k^\Phi(\rho)=(g^k)^\top d_{\mathrm{SQCQP}}^k+\rho\,DV(x^k)[d_{\mathrm{SQCQP}}^k]$ is strictly decreasing in \(\rho\). Since                               
\(\rho\leftarrow\gamma_\rho\rho\) with \(\gamma_\rho>1\), a finite number of penalty increases produces \(D_k^\Phi<0\).

It remains to consider an effective SQP direction. Feasibility of the linearized SQP constraints implies $DV(x^k)[d_{\mathrm{SQP}}^k]\leq -V(x^k).$ Hence, if \(V(x^k)>0\), and $DV(x^k)[d_{\mathrm{SQP}}^k]<0,$ and the same geometric penalty increase produces \(D_k^\Phi<0\) after finitely many updates whenever it is not already negative.

If \(V(x^k)=0\), the current point is feasible. Let 
\((\widehat{\lambda}_{\mathrm{SQP}}^k, \widehat{\mu}_{\mathrm{SQP}}^k)\)
be the SQP subproblem multipliers. Taking the inner product of the SQP stationarity condition with \(d_{\mathrm{SQP}}^k\), and using the linearized constraint equations and complementarity, gives
\[(g^k)^\top d_{\mathrm{SQP}}^k\leq-(d_{\mathrm{SQP}}^k)^\top
B^kd_{\mathrm{SQP}}^k.\] Assumption~\ref{ass:4.3} therefore yields
\[(g^k)^\top d_{\mathrm{SQP}}^k\leq-\underline b \|d_{\mathrm{SQP}}^k\|_2^2<0\]
whenever \(d_{\mathrm{SQP}}^k\neq0\). Since \(DV(x^k)[d_{\mathrm{SQP}}^k]\leq0\), it follows that \(D_k^\Phi<0\).

Thus, every nonzero effective direction either already satisfies the stochastic merit-descent condition or attains it after finitely many penalty adjustments. A numerically zero direction is treated separately by the exact KKT safeguard described in Section~\ref{subsec:method_globalization}.
head: environment

label: lem:4.5
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Armijo backtracking termination

title: Proof
body_md:
From Lemma~\ref{lem:4.3},\[\Phi(x^k+\alpha d^k;\rho_k)\leq\Phi(x^k;\rho_k)+\alpha D_k^\Phi+\alpha\|e^k\|_2\|d^k\|_2+C_\Phi^k\alpha^2\|d^k\|_2^2.\]
Using the assumed estimator-accuracy bound gives
\[\Phi(x^k+\alpha d^k;\rho_k)\leq\Phi(x^k;\rho_k)+\alpha(1-\vartheta)D_k^\Phi+
C_\Phi^k\alpha^2\|d^k\|_2^2.\]
Because \(D_k^\Phi<0\) and \(1-\sigma-\vartheta>0\), the Armijo condition
$\Phi(x^k+\alpha d^k;\rho_k)\leq\Phi(x^k;\rho_k)+\sigma\alpha D_k^\Phi$ is guaranteed whenever $C_\Phi^k\alpha\|d^k\|_2^2\leq(1-\sigma-\vartheta)(-D_k^\Phi).$
Thus, for \(d^k\neq0\), every sufficiently small positive step length satisfies the Armijo condition. Since the backtracking sequence 
\(\{1,\beta,\beta^2,\ldots\}\) tends to zero for \(0<\beta<1\), a finite accepted step \(\alpha_k>0\) exists.
head: environment

label: lem:4.6
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Boundedness of multiplier estimates

title: Proof
body_md:
Let \(\Omega\) denote the set of accumulation points of\(\{x^k\}\). By Assumption~\ref{ass:4.4}, \(\{x^k\}\subset\mathcal X\) for a compact set \(\mathcal X\);hence \(\Omega\) is compact.

Since each \(F_r\) is continuously differentiable on \(\mathcal X\),there exists \(M_F>0\) such that $\|\nabla F_r(x)\|_2\leq M_F,\qquad x\in\mathcal X,\quad r=1,\ldots,N.$ At refresh iterations \(g^k=\nabla F(x^k)\), while between two
successive refreshes the SPIDER recursion contains at most \(q-1\) increments, each satisfying\[\left\|\nabla F_{\mathcal B_k}(x^k)-\nabla F_{\mathcal B_k}(x^{k-1})\right\|_2\leq2M_F.\]
Therefore, there exists \(M_g<\infty\) such that $\|g^k\|_2\leq M_g$ for all \(k\).

By Assumption~\ref{ass:4.1} and compactness of \(\mathcal X\), the constraint values, Jacobians, and Hessians are uniformly bounded, while Assumption~\ref{ass:4.3} gives uniform bounds on \(B^k\) and \(G^k\). Hence all data entering the local SQP and SQCQP KKT systems remain bounded.

For every \(x^\star\in\Omega\), Assumption~\ref{ass:4.5} provides a neighborhood \(\mathcal U(x^\star)\) in which the relevant local KKT system is strongly regular with bounded inverse-Lipschitz modulus. Consequently, the corresponding primal--dual KKT pair$z^k=\begin{bmatrix}d^k\\\widehat{\nu}^k\end{bmatrix}$ is bounded whenever \(x^k\in\mathcal U(x^\star)\).

Since \(\Omega\) is compact, finitely many such neighborhoods cover \(\Omega\). The sequence \(\{x^k\}\) eventually lies in their union; otherwise, a subsequence outside the union would possess, by compactness of \(\mathcal X\), an accumulation point in \(\Omega\), yielding a contradiction. Taking the maximum of the finitely many local bounds therefore gives \(M_z<\infty\) and \(K_0\) such that
\[\left\|\begin{bmatrix}d^k\\\widehat{\nu}^k\end{bmatrix}\right\|_2\leq M_z,\qquad
k\geq K_0.\]
Thus the local multiplier components \(\widehat{\lambda}^k\) and \(\widehat{\mu}^k\) are uniformly bounded on the regular tail.
Finally, the multiplier handoff$\lambda^{k+1}=\widehat{\lambda}^k,\ \mu^{k+1}=\widehat{\mu}^k$ implies that the outer multiplier sequence inherits this boundedness. Hence there exist finite constants \(M_\lambda,M_\mu>0\) and an index \(K_\mu\) such that \ $\|\lambda^k\|_\infty\leq M_\lambda,\\|\mu^k\|_\infty\leq M_\mu,\ k\geq K_\mu,$
which proves \eqref{eq:multiplier_boundedness}.
head: environment

label: thm:4.1
title: Theorem
head: environment
name: Finite stabilization of the penalty parameter

title: Proof
body_md:
By Lemma~\ref{lem:4.6}, there exist finite constants \(M_\lambda,M_\mu>0\) and an index \(K_\mu\) such that the multiplier sequences are bounded for all \(k\geq K_\mu\). Define $M_\star=\max\{1,M_\lambda,M_\mu\}.$Hence, for all sufficiently large \(k\),\[\max\left\{1,\|\lambda^{k+1}\|_\infty,\|\mu^{k+1}\|_\infty\right\}
\leq M_\star.\]
Therefore, once $\rho_k\geq\gamma_\rho M_\star,$ the post-step multiplier update cannot increase the penalty.
By hypothesis, on the same regular tail no within-iteration increase is required whenever $\rho_k\geq\rho_{\mathrm{des}}.$ If \(\rho_k<\rho_{\mathrm{des}}\), the geometric update \(\rho\leftarrow\gamma_\rho\rho\) can overshoot this threshold by at most one factor \(\gamma_\rho\), so the resulting working penalty is smaller than $\gamma_\rho\rho_{\mathrm{des}}.$ Moreover, an SQCQP candidate satisfying
\(D_k^\Phi\geq0\) and \(DV(x^k)[d_{\mathrm{SQCQP}}^k]\geq0\) does not trigger indefinite penalty growth, since the algorithm switches to the SQP probe.

Now suppose  $K_0=\max\{K_\mu,K_{\mathrm{des}}\},\qquad\rho_\star=\max\left\{\rho_{K_0}, \gamma_\rho\rho_{\mathrm{des}},\gamma_\rho^2M_\star\right\}.$
The within-iteration adjustment cannot exceed \(\gamma_\rho\rho_{\mathrm{des}}\), while a post-step increase from \(\rho_k<\gamma_\rho M_\star\) gives
$\rho_{k+1}=\gamma_\rho\rho_k<\gamma_\rho^2M_\star.$

Thus\[\rho_k\leq\rho_\star,\qquad k\geq K_0.\]
Finally, \(\rho_k\) never decreases, and whenever it increases it is multiplied by the fixed factor \(\gamma_\rho>1\). Hence infinitely many increases would imply \(\rho_k\to\infty\), contradicting the finite upper bound \(\rho_\star\). Therefore only finitely many penalty increases are possible. Consequently, there exist
\(K_\rho<\infty\) and \(\bar\rho>0\) such that\[\rho_k=\bar\rho,\qquad k\geq K_\rho,\] which proves \eqref{eq:penalty_stabilization}.
head: environment

label: lem:4.7
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Uniform merit descent on the stabilized tail

title: Proof
body_md:
Since the penalty has stabilized, the post-step update and multiplier handoff imply $\|\widehat\lambda^k\|_\infty,\|\widehat\mu^k\|_\infty \leq\widehat M$ for all sufficiently large \(k\).

If \(d^k=d_{\mathrm{SQP}}^k\), equations \eqref{eq:sqp_kkt_system} yield
\[(g^k)^\top d^k=-(d^k)^\top B^kd^k+(\widehat\nu^k)^\top r^k\leq-\underline b\|d^k\|_2^2+\widehat M V(x^k).\]
Moreover, SQP linearized feasibility gives \(DV(x^k)[d^k]\leq-V(x^k)\).

Hence $D_k^\Phi\leq-\underline b\|d^k\|_2^2-\rho_{\mathrm{gap}}V(x^k).$
If \(d^k=d_{\mathrm{SQCQP}}^k\), the SQCQP KKT conditions, 
\(r^k+A^kd^k+q^k(d^k)=0\), and$(\widehat\nu^k)^\top q^k(d^k)=\frac12(d^k)^\top
H^k(\widehat\nu^k)d^k$ give \[(g^k)^\top d^k\leq-\left(\underline g-\frac12C_H\right)\|d^k\|_2^2+\widehat M V(x^k),\]
where we used $\|H^k(\widehat\nu^k)\|_2\leq C_H,\qquad(\widehat\nu^k)^\top r^k\leq\widehat M V(x^k).$ The quadratic constraint model also implies
\[DV(x^k)[d^k]\leq-V(x^k)+C_q\|d^k\|_2^2.\]
Therefore,
\[D_k^\Phi\leq-\kappa_Q\|d^k\|_2^2-\rho_{\mathrm{gap}}V(x^k).\]
Taking \(\kappa_\Phi=\min\{\underline b,\kappa_Q\}\) establishes \eqref{eq:uniform_merit_descent}. The SQP bound also applies when the globalization safeguard replaces an SQCQP candidate by the SQP probe.
head: environment

label: lem:4.8
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:4.8}
Suppose Assumptions~\ref{ass:4.1} and~\ref{ass:4.2} hold. If \(k+1\) is a non-refresh iteration, then \[\mathbb E\left[E^{k+1}\mid\mathcal F_k\right]\leq
E^k+\frac{L_F^2}{b_{k+1}}\alpha_k^2\|d^k\|_2^2.\]
If \(k+1\) is a refresh iteration, then $E^{k+1}=0.$
head: environment
name: Estimator-error energy recursion

title: Proof
body_md:
At a non-refresh iteration, Lemma~\ref{lem:4.1} gives$e^{k+1}=e^k+\xi^{k+1},\
\mathbb E\left[\xi^{k+1}\mid\mathcal F_k\right]=0.$
Hence
\[\begin{aligned}\mathbb E\left[E^{k+1}\mid\mathcal F_k\right]&=\mathbb E\left[
\|e^k+\xi^{k+1}\|_2^2\mid\mathcal F_k\right]\\&=E^k+\mathbb E\left[ \|\xi^{k+1}\|_2^2\mid\mathcal F_k\right],\end{aligned}\] because the conditional cross term vanishes.

By Lemma~\ref{lem:4.1}, and $x^{k+1}-x^k=\alpha_kd^k,$ the claimed recursion follows.If \(k+1\) is a refresh iteration, the SPIDER definition gives
$g^{k+1}=\nabla F(x^{k+1}),$ and therefore \(E^{k+1}=0\).
head: environment

label: thm:4.2
title: Theorem
head: environment
name: Coupled stochastic Lyapunov descent

title: Proof
body_md:
We consider separately a non-refresh transition and a refresh transition.
\medskip
\noindent
\textbf{Case 1: \(k+1\) is a non-refresh iteration.}
By Lemma~\ref{lem:4.5}, the Armijo backtracking is well defined on the considered tail. Hence 
\[\Phi(x^{k+1};\bar\rho)\leq\Phi(x^k;\bar\rho)+\sigma\alpha_kD_k^\Phi.\]
Using Lemma~\ref{lem:4.7},
\[\Phi(x^{k+1};\bar\rho)\leq\Phi(x^k;\bar\rho)-\sigma\kappa_\Phi\alpha_k\|d^k\|_2^2
-\sigma\rho_{\mathrm{gap}}\alpha_kV(x^k).\]

At the same transition, Lemma~\ref{lem:4.8} gives
\[\mathbb E\left[E^{k+1}\mid\mathcal F_k\right]\leq E^k+\frac{L_F^2}{b_{k+1}}
\alpha_k^2\|d^k\|_2^2.\]
Multiplying by \(C_{r_{k+1}}\), adding the merit estimate, and using the definition of \(\Psi^k\) yields
\[\begin{aligned}\mathbb E\left[\Psi^{k+1}\mid\mathcal F_k\right]\leq{}&\Psi^k
-\left(C_{r_k}-C_{r_{k+1}}\right)E^k-\sigma\kappa_\Phi\alpha_k\|d^k\|_2^2\\&+
C_{r_{k+1}}\frac{L_F^2}{b_{k+1}}\alpha_k^2\|d^k\|_2^2-\sigma\rho_{\mathrm{gap}}
\alpha_kV(x^k).\end{aligned}\]
Since $C_{r_k}-C_{r_{k+1}}=\omega,\qquad C_{r_{k+1}}\leq q\omega,\qquad b_{k+1}\geq b_0, \qquad 0<\alpha_k\leq1,$
we have
\[C_{r_{k+1}}\frac{L_F^2}{b_{k+1}}\alpha_k^2\leqq\omega\frac{L_F^2}{b_0}\alpha_k
\leq\frac{\sigma\kappa_\Phi}{2}\alpha_k.\]
Therefore,
\[\begin{aligned}\mathbb E\left[\Psi^{k+1}\mid\mathcal F_k\right]\leq{}&\Psi^k-
\frac{\sigma\kappa_\Phi}{2}\alpha_k\|d^k\|_2^2-\omega E^k\\&-\sigma\rho_{\mathrm{gap}}\alpha_kV(x^k).\end{aligned}\]
\medskip
\noindent
\textbf{Case 2: \(k+1\) is a refresh iteration.}
In this case, $E^{k+1}=0,$ and $C_{r_k}=\omega.$

The Armijo decrease and Lemma~\ref{lem:4.7} give
\[\Phi(x^{k+1};\bar\rho)\leq\Phi(x^k;\bar\rho)-\sigma\kappa_\Phi\alpha_k\|d^k\|_2^2
-\sigma\rho_{\mathrm{gap}}\alpha_kV(x^k).\]
Therefore,
\[\begin{aligned}\Psi^{k+1}&=\Phi(x^{k+1};\bar\rho)\\&\leq\Psi^k-\omega E^k-
\sigma\kappa_\Phi\alpha_k\|d^k\|_2^2-\sigma\rho_{\mathrm{gap}}\alpha_kV(x^k).
\end{aligned}\]
Since $\sigma\kappa_\Phi\geq\frac{\sigma\kappa_\Phi}{2},$ the same bound obtained in the non-refresh case also holds here.This proves \eqref{eq:coupled_lyapunov_descent}.
head: environment

label: cor:4.2
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:4.2}
Under the conditions of Theorem~\ref{thm:4.2},
\[\sum_{k=K_L}^{\infty}\alpha_k\|d^k\|_2^2<\infty,\qquad\sum_{k=K_L}^{\infty}
E^k<\infty,\qquad\sum_{k=K_L}^{\infty}\alpha_kV(x^k)<\infty\qquad\text{a.s.}\]
Consequently,
\[\sum_{k=K_L}^{\infty}\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|_2^2<\infty\qquad\text{a.s.},\ \ and \quad
\|g^k-\nabla F(x^k)\|_2\longrightarrow0\qquad\text{a.s.}\]
head: environment
name: Almost-sure summability and estimator consistency

title: Proof
body_md:
By Assumption~\ref{ass:4.4}, \(x^k\) remains in the compact set \(\mathcal X\). Hence \(\Phi(x;\bar\rho)\) is bounded below on \(\mathcal X\), and since \(E^k\geq0\), so is \(\Psi^k\). Applying the Robbins--Siegmund theorem to
\eqref{eq:coupled_lyapunov_descent} yields the almost-sure summability of its three nonnegative descent terms.

Furthermore,
\[\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|_2^2=\alpha_k^2\|d^k\|_2^2\leq\alpha_k\|d^k\|_2^2,\]
so the iterate increments are square summable. Finally, \(E^k=\|g^k-\nabla F(x^k)\|_2^2\), and summability of the nonnegative sequence \(\{E^k\}\) implies \(E^k\to0\) almost surely, proving the estimator-consistency conclusion.
head: environment

label: lem:4.9
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Uniform lower bound on accepted step sizes

title: Proof
body_md:
By Theorem~\ref{thm:4.1}, the penalty parameter is constant on the relevant tail:$\rho_k=\bar\rho.$ Hence Lemma~\ref{lem:4.3} admits the uniform quadratic-remainder constant $C_\Phi=\frac{L_F}{2}+\frac{\bar\rho}{2}\left(mM_h+pM_c \right).$

Moreover, Lemma~\ref{lem:4.7} gives $-D_k^\Phi\geq \kappa_\Phi\|d^k\|_2^2+\rho_{\mathrm{gap}}V(x^k)\geq\kappa_\Phi\|d^k\|_2^2.$
By the estimator-accuracy condition used in Lemma~\ref{lem:4.5}, there exists
\(0\leq\vartheta<1-\sigma\) such that $\|e^k\|_2\|d^k\|_2\leq\vartheta(-D_k^\Phi)$
on the relevant tail. Therefore the stochastic merit-remainder boundimplies
\[\Phi(x^k+\alpha d^k;\bar\rho)\leq\Phi(x^k;\bar\rho)+\alpha(1-\vartheta)D_k^\Phi+
C_\Phi\alpha^2\|d^k\|_2^2.\]
Consequently, the Armijo condition is guaranteed whenever
\[C_\Phi\alpha\|d^k\|_2^2\leq(1-\sigma-\vartheta)(-D_k^\Phi).\]
Using $-D_k^\Phi\geq\kappa_\Phi\|d^k\|_2^2,$
it is sufficient that\[\alpha\leq\frac{(1-\sigma-\vartheta)\kappa_\Phi}{C_\Phi}.\]

By Lemma~\ref{lem:4.6}, the effective directions are bounded on the regular tail. Since \(\mathcal X\subset\mathcal N\), with \(\mathcal X\) compact and \(\mathcal N\) open, there exists a uniform \(\bar\alpha>0\) such that all trial segments
$x^k+\alpha d^k,\ 0\leq\alpha\leq\bar\alpha,$ remain in the neighborhood where the remainder estimate is valid.

Define \[\alpha_\star=\min\left\{1,\bar\alpha,\frac{(1-\sigma-\vartheta)\kappa_\Phi}{C_\Phi}\right\}>0.\]
Every trial step satisfying \(\alpha\leq\alpha_\star\) therefore satisfies the Armijo condition.

Since backtracking tests $1,\beta,\beta^2,\ldots,\ \ 0<\beta<1,$ the first accepted step satisfies $\alpha_k\geq\beta\alpha_\star.$
Thus \eqref{eq:uniform_step_lower_bound} holds with
\[\underline\alpha=\beta\alpha_\star>0.\]
head: environment

label: lem:4.10
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Vanishing direction and primal infeasibility

title: Proof
body_md:
Corollary~\ref{cor:4.2} gives $\sum_{k=K_L}^{\infty}\alpha_k\|d^k\|_2^2<\infty\ a.s.$ and $\sum_{k=K_L}^{\infty}\alpha_kV(x^k)<\infty\ a.s.$

By Lemma~\ref{lem:4.9},$\alpha_k\geq\underline\alpha>0$ for all sufficiently large \(k\). Hence \[\underline\alpha\sum_{k=K_\alpha}^{\infty}\|d^k\|_2^2\leq \sum_{k=K_\alpha}^{\infty}\alpha_k\|d^k\|_2^2<\infty.\]
Therefore $\|d^k\|_2\longrightarrow0\qquad\text{a.s.}$

Similarly,\[\underline\alpha\sum_{k=K_\alpha}^{\infty}V(x^k)\leq \sum_{k=K_\alpha}^{\infty}\alpha_kV(x^k)<\infty.\]
Since \(V(x^k)\geq0\),\[V(x^k)\longrightarrow0\qquad\text{a.s.}\]
By the definition $V(x)=\|h(x)\|_1+\|c(x)^+\|_1,$ both nonnegative terms must converge to zero, which proves the result.
head: environment

label: lem:4.11
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Asymptotic dual feasibility and complementarity

title: Proof
body_md:
The inequality multipliers of each local SQP or SQCQP subproblem satisfy $\widehat{\mu}^k\geq0.$ Since the accepted local multiplier pair is handed directly to the outer sequence, $\mu^{k+1}=\widehat{\mu}^k,$ dual feasibility is inherited by the outer multipliers.

It remains to establish complementary slackness. Let \(\widehat c_j^k(d^k)\) denote the local model of the \(j\)-th inequality constraint associated with the effective direction:
\[ \widehat{c}_j^k(d^k) = c_j(x^k) + \nabla c_j(x^k)^\top d^k \quad \text{in SQP mode, and} \]
\[ \widehat{c}_j^k(d^k) = c_j(x^k) + \nabla c_j(x^k)^\top d^k + \frac{1}{2} (d^k)^\top \nabla^2 c_j(x^k) d^k \quad \text{in SQCQP mode.} \]

The local KKT complementarity condition gives $\widehat\mu_j^k\widehat c_j^k(d^k)=0.$ Consequently, in either mode,
\[\left|\widehat\mu_j^k c_j(x^k)\right|\leq|\widehat\mu_j^k|\left(\|\nabla c_j(x^k)\|_2\|d^k\|_2+\frac12M_c\|d^k\|_2^2\right),\]
where the quadratic term is absent in SQP mode.

By Lemma~\ref{lem:4.6}, the local multipliers are uniformly bounded, and by Lemma~\ref{lem:4.10},\[d^k\longrightarrow0.\]
Hence \[\widehat\mu^k\odot c(x^k)\longrightarrow0.\]

Using multiplier handoff,$\mu^{k+1}=\widehat\mu^k.$ and $x^{k+1}-x^k=\alpha_kd^k
\longrightarrow0$ moreover \(c\) is continuously differentiable on the compact relevant region, $c(x^{k+1})-c(x^k)\longrightarrow0.$
Therefore
\[\begin{aligned}\mu^{k+1}\odot c(x^{k+1})&=\widehat\mu^k\odot c(x^k)\ +\
\widehat\mu^k\odot\left(c(x^{k+1})-c(x^k)\right)\longrightarrow0,\end{aligned}\]
because \(\widehat\mu^k\) is bounded. Shifting the index proves \eqref{eq:complementarity_residual_zero}.
head: environment

label: thm:4.3
title: Theorem
head: environment
name: Global KKT convergence

title: Proof
body_md:
Lemma~\ref{lem:4.10} gives \[h(x^k)\longrightarrow0,\qquad c(x^k)^+\longrightarrow0 \qquad\text{a.s.}\]
Thus the primal-feasibility blocks of the KKT residual vanish.
Lemma~\ref{lem:4.11} gives \[\mu^k\geq0\]
and \[\mu^k\odot c(x^k)\longrightarrow0\qquad\text{a.s.}\]
It remains only to establish stationarity.

Let $(\widehat\lambda^k,\widehat\mu^k)$ be the local multiplier pair corresponding to the effective direction \(d^k\). The stationarity condition of the effective local subproblem is written as
\[g^k+J_h(x^k)^\top\widehat\lambda^k+J_c(x^k)^\top\widehat\mu^k+Q^k d^k+
r_{\mathrm{curv}}^k=0,\] where
\[Q^k=\begin{cases}B^k,&\text{for an effective SQP direction},\\G^k,&\text{for an effective SQCQP direction},\end{cases}\]
and\[r_{\mathrm{curv}}^k=\begin{cases}0,&\text{for SQP},\\H^k(\widehat\nu^k)d^k,
&\text{for SQCQP}.\end{cases}\]

By Assumption~\ref{ass:4.3}, both \(B^k\) and \(G^k\) are uniformly bounded. Hence Lemma~\ref{lem:4.10} gives $Q^k d^k\longrightarrow0.$ By Lemma~\ref{lem:4.6} and Assumption~\ref{ass:4.1}, $\|H^k(\widehat\nu^k)\|_2\leq C_H$ on the relevant tail, and consequently \[r_{\mathrm{curv}}^k\longrightarrow0.\]
It follows that\[g^k+J_h(x^k)^\top\widehat\lambda^k+J_c(x^k)^\top\widehat\mu^k
\longrightarrow0.\]

Using Corollary~\ref{cor:4.2} we get,\[\nabla F(x^k)+J_h(x^k)^\top\widehat\lambda^k+J_c(x^k)^\top\widehat\mu^k\longrightarrow0.\]

After the accepted step, the multiplier handoff gives
$\lambda^{k+1}=\widehat\lambda^k,\ \mu^{k+1}= \widehat\mu^k.$
Furthermore,$x^{k+1}-x^k=\alpha_kd^k\longrightarrow0.$
The continuity of \(\nabla F\), \(J_h\), and \(J_c\), together with the boundedness of the multipliers, therefore gives
\[\begin{aligned}&\nabla F(x^{k+1})+J_h(x^{k+1})^\top\lambda^{k+1}+ J_c(x^{k+1})^\top\mu^{k+1} \longrightarrow0.\end{aligned}\]
Hence \[\left\|\nabla_x\mathcal L (x^{k+1},\lambda^{k+1},\mu^{k+1})\right\|_2\longrightarrow0,\]
and shifting the index yields
\[\left\|\nabla_x\mathcal L(x^k,\lambda^k,\mu^k)\right\|_2\longrightarrow0.\]

Thus every block of \eqref{eq:kkt_residual} converges to zero almost surely. This proves\eqref{eq:global_kkt_residual}.

Finally, Assumption~\ref{ass:4.4} and Lemma~\ref{lem:4.6} imply boundedness of the primal--dual sequence. Hence accumulation points exist. Let
$(x^{k_j},\lambda^{k_j},\mu^{k_j})\longrightarrow(x^\star,\lambda^\star,\mu^\star).$
Passing to the limit in the four vanishing KKT-residual blocks gives
\[\nabla_x\mathcal L(x^\star,\lambda^\star,\mu^\star)=0,\]
\[h(x^\star)=0,\qquad c(x^\star)\leq0,\]
and
\[\mu^\star\geq0,\qquad\mu^\star\odot c(x^\star)=0.\]
Therefore every accumulation point is a KKT point almost surely.
head: environment

label: lem:4.12
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Vanishing SQP probe

title: Proof
body_md:
Consider an almost-sure sample path on which the conclusions of Theorem~\ref{thm:4.3} and Corollary~\ref{cor:4.2} hold.In particular,
\[\left\|R_{\mathrm{KKT}}(x^k,\lambda^k,\mu^k)\right\|_2\longrightarrow0\]
and \[g^k-\nabla F(x^k)\longrightarrow0.\]
Suppose, to the contrary, that \(\|d_{\mathrm{SQP}}^k\|_2\not\to0\). Then there exist \(\varepsilon_d>0\) and an infinite subsequence \(\{k_j\}\) such that
\[\|d_{\mathrm{SQP}}^{k_j}\|_2\geq\varepsilon_d.\]
By Assumption~\ref{ass:4.4}, the primal sequence lies in the compact set \(\mathcal X\). By Lemma~\ref{lem:4.6}, the multiplier sequences are bounded. Hence, after passing to a further subsequence if necessary,
\[x^{k_j}\longrightarrow x^\star,\qquad \lambda^{k_j}\longrightarrow\lambda^\star,
\qquad \mu^{k_j}\longrightarrow\mu^\star.\]
Theorem~\ref{thm:4.3} then implies that \((x^\star,\lambda^\star,\mu^\star)\) is a KKT point.

Moreover,\[g^{k_j}=\nabla F(x^{k_j})+e^{k_j}\longrightarrow\nabla F(x^\star).\]
Since there are only finitely many possible active sets, a further subsequence may be chosen on which the locally identified active set is fixed. Assumption~\ref{ass:4.5} gives strong regularity of the corresponding local SQP KKT system with a uniformly bounded inverse-Lipschitz modulus.

At the limiting KKT point, the SQP subproblem admits the zero direction
as the local solution. Indeed, $h(x^\star)=0,\ c_{\mathcal A^\star}(x^\star)=0,$
and the KKT stationarity condition gives
\[\nabla F(x^\star)+J_h(x^\star)^\top\lambda^\star+J_{c_{\mathcal A^\star}}(x^\star)^\top\mu_{\mathcal A^\star}^\star=0.\]
Thus $d_{\mathrm{SQP}}^\star=0$ solves the limiting SQP KKT system.

By strong regularity, the locally relevant SQP primal--dual solution
depends Lipschitz continuously on the local problem data. Since those
data converge to their limiting KKT values along the selected
subsequence, $d_{\mathrm{SQP}}^{k_j}\longrightarrow d_{\mathrm{SQP}}^\star=0.$

This contradicts $\|d_{\mathrm{SQP}}^{k_j}\|_2\geq\varepsilon_d.$ Therefore
\[\|d_{\mathrm{SQP}}^k\|_2\longrightarrow0\qquad\text{a.s.}\]
head: environment

label: lem:4.13
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Vanishing RCMCI

title: Proof
body_md:
By Assumption~\ref{ass:4.1}, the constraint Hessians are uniformly bounded. Hence, for every equality and inequality constraint, \[|q_{h_i,k}|\leq\frac{M_h}{2}\|d_{\mathrm{SQP}}^k\|_2^2,\qquad |q_{c_j,k}| \leq \frac{M_c}{2}\|d_{\mathrm{SQP}}^k\|_2^2.\]
Since every RCMCI normalization scale is bounded below by \(\epsilon_s>0\), it follows that
\[0\leq\eta_k\leq\frac{M_{\mathrm{curv}}}{2\epsilon_s}\|d_{\mathrm{SQP}}^k\|_2^2,
\qquad M_{\mathrm{curv}}:=\max\{M_h,M_c\}.\]
Lemma~\ref{lem:4.12} therefore implies $\eta_k\longrightarrow0\qquad\text{a.s.}$

For the smoothed indicator,\[\bar\eta_k=\beta_\eta\bar\eta_{k-1} +(1-\beta_\eta)\eta_k,\qquad 0\leq\beta_\eta<1.\]
Iterating from any \(K\) gives \[\bar\eta_k=\beta_\eta^{\,k-K+1}\bar\eta_{K-1}+(1-\beta_\eta)\sum_{\ell=K}^{k} \beta_\eta^{\,k-\ell}\eta_\ell.\]
Since \(\eta_\ell\to0\) almost surely and the geometric weights have
total mass at most one, the second term tends to zero, while the first
vanishes because \(\beta_\eta<1\). Hence $\bar\eta_k\longrightarrow0\qquad\text{a.s.}$
head: environment

label: thm:4.4
title: Theorem
head: environment
name: Eventual SQP selection

title: Proof
body_md:
By Lemma~\ref{lem:4.13}, $\bar{\eta}_k\longrightarrow0\qquad\text{a.s.} \ $
and the lower hysteresis threshold satisfies $\eta_{\mathrm{low}}>0.$
Therefore, on every sample path for which \(\bar{\eta}_k\to0\), there exists a finite index \(K_{\mathrm{switch}}\) such that $\bar{\eta}_k\leq\eta_{\mathrm{low}},\ k\geq K_{\mathrm{switch}}.$
By the RCMCI switching rule, this implies \[\mathcal M_k=\mathrm{SQP}\]
for every \(k\geq K_{\mathrm{switch}}\).

Since the globalization safeguard can replace an SQCQP candidate by
the SQP probe but does not replace an SQP preference by an SQCQP
direction, eventual SQP preference also implies eventual SQP effective
mode.
head: environment

label: cor:4.3
title: Corollary
head: environment
name: Vanishing asymptotic SQCQP frequency

title: Proof
body_md:
By Theorem~\ref{thm:4.4}, there exists a finite random index 
\(K_{\mathrm{switch}}\) after which the RCMCI always selects SQP. Hence
$N_{\mathrm{SQCQP}}(K)\leq K_{\mathrm{switch}}$ for all sufficiently large \(K\). Therefore,\[0\leq\frac{N_{\mathrm{SQCQP}}(K)}{K}\leq\frac{K_{\mathrm{switch}}}{K}
\longrightarrow0\qquad\text{a.s.}\]
